raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With speculative decoding, the default CUDA graph sizes now include every decode batch of 1 to 8 requests. Small
batches stop padding to the next power of two, which runs 1 + K extra tokens per padded request through every
layer.

## Claims

- With MTP K=3, 3, 5 and 7 running requests replay 12-, 20- and 28-token graphs instead of 16, 24 and 32. GLM-5.2-
  NVFP4, TP4, B300: decode -6% to -7% at 3 requests, -2.5% to -3.4% at 5, -2.2% to -2.4% at 7, unchanged at 1.
- Three extra decode graphs (and their piecewise twins) for K=3: capture 6 s -> 7 s, graph memory 0.61 -> 0.65 GiB per GPU.
- Without speculation, and for explicit `cudagraph_capture_sizes`, nothing changes.
- On InferenceX AgentX, GLM-5.3 vs SGLang: decode time on the same turns drops 0.5-0.9% at concurrency 1-8 and 0.1% at 16 on 4x GB200 (0.5-1.1% on 4x B300); batches of 3-7 running requests are a small share of AgentX decode steps.

## Validation

- `tests/compile/test_config.py -k keep_all_sizes_bounded` (expected request grid updated) and
  `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py` pass. On B300, `tests/compile/test_config.py -k cudagraph` has 12
  failures, the same 12 as on main on that machine (`unchanged_without_speculation`, `respects_platform_ceiling`,
  `still_clamped_by_token_budget`, `test_use_cudagraphs`), so unrelated to this change.
- End to end: B300 x4 (SM103), GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP4, MTP K=3 with synthetic acceptance length 3.0 (fixed step count),
  `max_model_len` 1M, FP8 KV, default CUDA graph sizes. Decode ms/token per request, median of 9 repetitions of
  (T1200 - T200) / 1000 on cached prompts:

  | context | requests | before | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 25K | 1 | 3.094 | 3.097 |
  | 25K | 3 | 4.300 | 3.991 (-7.2%) |
  | 25K | 5 | 5.134 | 5.007 (-2.5%) |
  | 25K | 7 | 5.662 | 5.540 (-2.2%) |
  | 94K | 1 | 3.131 | 3.119 |
  | 94K | 3 | 4.370 | 4.097 (-6.2%) |
  | 94K | 5 | 5.265 | 5.087 (-3.4%) |
  | 94K | 7 | 5.788 | 5.647 (-2.4%) |

  (Measured on top of other GLM-5 decode changes; this PR touches only the capture sizes.) On GB200 with an
  explicit list of every request count up to 32, 3 requests went from 4.145 to 3.944 ms/token at 40K and AgentX
  c=8 throughput rose 1.7%.

<details>
<summary>InferenceX AgentX setup and full results (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, vLLM vs SGLang)</summary>

InferenceX c801c9f2d AgentX scenario (pinned AIPerf), 20-minute fast mode, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 rev e3b8f9f2, TP4, MTP 3
(synthetic acceptance 2.99), native KV offload 135 GB per rank, Rust frontend, MoE autotune, `max-num-seqs` =
2 x concurrency. vLLM is main dcd07967ca with its default linear backend and default CUDA graph config, plus the
PRs cumulatively. SGLang a916d91cd3 with IMEX, TRT-LLM all-reduce fusion, `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`. Fresh
server per point, SGLang and the four vLLM variants alternating per concurrency. "Decode" is request latency minus
TTFT, summed over the turns both runs finished (a few hundred per point); fast-mode throughput alone moves about
+-2% between runs.

4x GB200 (c=1/4 on driver 580.173.02; c=8/16 on 580.178.04 after a host reinstall, SGLang rerun there too):

| decode time vs SGLang, same turns | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6630, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6631, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6632) | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 | +8.9% | +5.8% | +4.0% | +3.2% |
| c=4 | +12.7% | +10.6% | +7.3% | +7.3% |
| c=8 | +12.3% | +9.5% | +7.9% | +7.3% |
| c=16 | -22.6% | -25.0% | -24.5% | -24.3% |

| tok/s/GPU vs SGLang | main | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c=1 (SGLang 5,681) | -3.2% | -0.4% | -1.1% | +0.6% |
| c=4 (SGLang 6,783) | -0.6% | -2.4% | +0.4% | -1.7% |
| c=8 (SGLang 11,799) | -11.5% | -9.4% | -8.8% | -8.4% |
| c=16 (SGLang 10,529) | +44.7% | +45.6% | +45.8% | +46.8% |

| decode time vs the previous column, same turns | + #62170, #62171, #62172 | + #62174 | + #62173 |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 c=1 / c=4 / c=8 / c=16 | -2.9% / -2.0% / -2.1% / -2.9% | -1.6% / -3.1% / -1.2% / -0.4% | -0.8% / -0.9% / -0.5% / -0.1% |
| B300 c=1 / c=4 | -2.5% / -4.1% | -1.6% / -3.1% | -0.5% / -1.1% |

#62170, #62171 and #62172 were measured together; `vllm bench forward` (target verify forward, spread < 0.1%)
splits their gain about 1/6, 1/2 and 1/3.

</details>

## Details

For speculative decoding, `_set_cudagraph_sizes` appends a request-count grid times `decode_query_len` (1 + K).
That grid started 1, 2, 4, 8, copied from the one-token grid, where padding 3 requests to 4 costs one token. A
decode request is 1 + K tokens, so the same padding costs 1 + K tokens. Padded tokens still go through the
attention, the GEMMs and the MoE (routed like real tokens), and at small batches decode is bound by those layers.
The token grid's 8-token stride already yields even request counts at K=3, so this adds 3, 5 and 7 requests there.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -692,7 +692,7 @@ def test_default_cudagraph_capture_sizes_keep_all_sizes_bounded():
     token_grid += list(range(256, token_grid_max + 1, 16))
 
     max_request_count = min(max_num_seqs, default_max_graph_size)
-    request_counts = [count for count in [1, 2, 4] if count <= max_request_count]
+    request_counts = list(range(1, min(max_request_count, 8) + 1))
     request_counts += list(range(8, min(max_request_count + 1, 256), 8))
     request_counts += list(range(256, max_request_count + 1, 16))
     request_counts.append(max_request_count)

@@ -2380,9 +2380,10 @@ def _set_cudagraph_sizes(self):
 
         `max_num_batched_tokens` is also appended to the list if it fits
         within `max_cudagraph_capture_size`, so the max batch size is captured
-        even when off-stride. Uniform decode sizes are appended when they fit
-        within the platform's default capture ceiling, since they need not land
-        on an 8- or 16-token stride.
+        even when off-stride. Uniform decode sizes (every request count up to
+        8, then 8- and 16-request strides, times the decode query length) are
+        appended when they fit within the platform's default capture ceiling,
+        since they need not land on an 8- or 16-token stride.
 
         In the end, `vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_capture_sizes`
         will be the final sizes to capture cudagraph (in ascending order).
@@ -2456,7 +2457,9 @@ def request_counts(max_reqs: int) -> list[int]:
                         # At most the platform default number of requests,
                         # mirroring the one-token-per-request decode ceiling.
                         max_reqs = min(max_reqs, default_max_graph_size)
-                        counts = [n for n in (1, 2, 4) if n <= max_reqs]
+                        # Every count up to 8: a padded request costs
+                        # decode_query_len tokens in every GEMM and MoE.
+                        counts = list(range(1, min(max_reqs, 8) + 1))
                         counts += list(range(8, min(max_reqs + 1, 256), 8))
                         counts += list(range(256, max_reqs + 1, 16))
                         return sorted(set(counts + [max_reqs]))
